findings.message: The new table `time.setting` has a personal column `updated_by` (it holds the acting person's id or name, written by `by(ctx)`). `modules/time/module.ts` has no 032 retention entry for `time.setting`. The module standard requires a retention entry for every personal-data table, and `*_by` columns are named as personal. Without one, erasure requests and legal holds never reach the person who last changed the rules. Fix: add a retention entry with `updated_by` in `subject` and `fields`, or keep the row with a stated reason.
findings.scenario: Admin Sahan changes the timesheet rules, then Sahan's erasure is approved → `time.setting.updated_by` still holds Sahan's identity, and the request never lists it.

findings.message: `reaches(v, entity)` is true when *any* of the viewer's role assignments is unscoped or covers the entity. It does not check the assignment that grants `time:approve`. The manager path in `chainFor` (and its copy in `hours-scope.ts:22`) is `canEver(time:approve) && reaches(...)`. So a manager whose approving role is scoped to entity A still reaches a report in entity B through an unscoped base role such as Employee. The 071 entity narrowing is bypassed for managers. Fix: only count assignments whose role grants `time:approve` (or Admin), and add that case to the entity-scope test.
findings.scenario: Viewer has Engineer (APPROVE) with legal_entity_ids=[A] and Employee unscoped. A direct report's `legal_entity_id` is B → `chainFor` returns "manager", so the viewer approves or rejects the week and sees it on Team time and in utilisation.

findings.message: A partial time read now sets `timeIncomplete` and flags people `overtime-unknown`. A time read that did not happen at all does neither. Three cases all go through `none(...)`: a drafter without `time:totals` (ForbiddenError), a system draft, and a viewerless context. Each returns empty hours with `unreadable` empty, so the run shows no warning chip and no per-person flag. "Could not ask" reads the same as "no overtime", and HR or Finance approve a run that silently left out approved overtime. Fix: in these branches, mark every person in `userIds` unreadable (or set `timeIncomplete`).
findings.scenario: An Admin or HR drafter without `time:totals` drafts October. Kasun has an approved 46 h week → no overtime line, no `overtime-unknown` flag, no warning chip; only a plain grey Sources sentence.

findings.message: The replay check compares project, day, hours and billable, but not `note`, which is part of the input. A retry with the same `clientRef` and a different note returns `replayed: true` instead of the refusal that README and AC-8 promise ("other input is refused"). The new note is silently dropped. The idempotency test has no note case. Fix: compare the stored note (and `agent`) too, and add the case to the test table.
findings.scenario: `log_time {FLT, 2026-10-27, 2h, clientRef: r1, note: 'API'}`, then the same call with `note: 'Release notes'` → returns `{id, replayed: true}`; the entry keeps note 'API' and no error is raised.

findings.message: The repeated-push filter covers only GitHub's `distinct` flag. Azure DevOps `git.push` events for a commit already pushed on another branch still pass through. Each push runs `draftCommitTime` again (a second activity line and a second pending suggestion), because time's handler dedups only commits that are already *logged*. Fix: dedup per commit id for every provider, for example in `draftCommitTime` or by checking time's pending suggestions by `source_ref`.
findings.scenario: Azure DevOps: commit X with 'CON-014 T3 done\nTime: 1.5h' is pushed to feature/x, then to main before anyone accepts → two 'Add 1.5 h on CON' suggestions and two 'drafted 1.5 h' activity lines.

findings.message: When two suggestions for the same commit are accepted at once, the loser's insert hits the unique index. `logEntry` then throws a plain `Error('already logged from the same source')` instead of resolving as `alreadyLogged`, so the second accept fails and the suggestion stays open. The test only checks the entry count, under `allSettled`. Fix: catch `source_taken` in `apply`, re-read with `bySource`, and resolve as `alreadyLogged`.
findings.scenario: Two pending drafts for commit e11c2f6b8 are accepted concurrently → one entry is logged (correct), but the second accept returns an error and its suggestion remains pending.

findings.message: `hoursVisibleTo` writes Time's visibility rule a second time, and its project-manager path is wider than `seesWeek`. It grants the whole person for the whole range if they have any hours on a managed project in that range. Time's own reads (`seesWeek`, `weekTotals`, `weeklyHours`) grant only the weeks that contain hours on that project. This breaks the reports README's own rule that a report is 'never wider than the source modules'. Fix: in the PM path, return only the hours in weeks that `seesWeek` lets the viewer see, for example by keying visibility on user and week. Don't keep a separate month-wide rule.
findings.scenario: In October, Nimal logs 1 h on FLT (managed by Sahan) in W41 and 40 h/week on CON in W42–W44. Sahan, as PM, calls get_utilisation for October and sees all of Nimal's logged and billable hours, while weekTotals(W43) for Sahan leaves Nimal out.

findings.message: The colleague-refusal assertion accepts either `null` or a 'forbidden' message, so it stays green whichever contract `get_person_utilisation` follows. The tool description now promises null. Assert null. Similarly, `entity-scope.test.ts` asserts `decideRequest(...).rejects.toThrow()` with no message, so any error passes.
The comment still describes hours visibility here, but the function moved to time's `hoursVisibleTo`. Move the comment to `inputs.ts` or drop it.

The new entry-rule refusals are thrown as plain `Error`: `allocationRefusal` and `dateRefusal` in `logEntry`, `writeCorrection`, `guardOwnDate` (correct.ts) and `requestChange` (request.ts). They have no `code` and no `retryable: false`. `userFacing()` (packages/mcp/src/registry.ts:23) rejects them, so REST and other reporters show an 'internal' error and hide the message, including its list of allowed projects. The same class was fixed for `guardShown` in 070. Fix: throw `ToolError(..., 'invalid_input')`, or set `retryable: false`, wherever a rule refuses.
findings.scenario: With requireAllocation on, POST /api/v1/tools/log_time {projectKey:'HRI'} → 500 internal with a reference, instead of 'not allocated to HR Insights in October; allocated to Fleet Tracker and Contoso Portal'.

findings.message: For an Admin scoped to one legal entity, `scopeSql` returns `true`, because `can()` without an entity doesn't narrow. `pageRequests` therefore fetches 51 requests from every entity and then drops the out-of-entity rows in JS. A page can come back empty or short with `truncated: true`, and each row costs an extra `entityOf` query. Fix: add the entity narrowing to the SQL (for example, a join to auth.user filtered on the assignment's legal_entity_ids).
findings.scenario: An Admin scoped to LK, where the 50 newest requests belong to AU staff → get_change_requests returns { requests: [], truncated: true }.

findings.message: `allocationRefusal` reads allocations with `contextFor.job` (system), not as the viewer. The refusal it returns names every project the person is allocated to that month, and it is shown to whoever logs or moves the entry. When that is a PM fixing someone else's entry, they see allocations outside their own allocations scope. Fix: read as the viewer, or leave the project list out when the actor isn't the owner.
findings.scenario: A PM moves Tharushi's entry to HRI → the refusal lists all of her October allocations, including projects the PM can't see in Allocations.
